Subject: Request: adjust uptime/remedy budget for CloudTerra pilot

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the performance profile looks promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with a formal ask around the SLA template before we move to the pilot PO. Two items they want adjusted for the pilot period (3 months):

1) Uptime target: CloudTerra is asking to lower the baseline uptime from 99.95% to 99.9% for the pilot window to account for our bursty test traffic and acceptance of limited fallback behavior.
2) Monthly remedy cap: we need a more predictable monthly remediation cap tied to committed spend — procurement would like a hard cap of $10k/month (rather than percentage-of-invoice).

We attached a short redline (CloudTerra_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf) with markup. Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept these two temporary concessions for the pilot, and if not, propose an alternative we can present internally?

Goal is to get procurement sign-off by next Friday (20 Aug). Happy to jump on a short call if useful.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Integrations, CloudTerra

Jordan — thanks for the note and for sending the redlines. Quick thoughts inline below.

On lowering the uptime to 99.9%: we generally push for 99.95% as the baseline for hosted customers. That said, for short pilots we can consider a temporary operational tolerance if accompanied by clear maintenance carveouts and fallbacks. I don’t want CloudTerra to be exposed to excessive risk; if Redwood accepts 99.9% for three months, we will require the following:
- explicit maintenance window carveouts (max 6 hours/month, scheduled and notified 72 hours prior),
- automatic fallback to a slightly smaller model variant (no data loss, degraded latency) rather than request drops, and
- a mutual exit clause if production traffic patterns differ drastically.

On the remedy cap: Redwood prefers remedy expressed as a percentage of monthly invoice for alignment, but we can provide a hard cap for the pilot. Proposed compromise: set the cap at the lesser of $10k or 20% of the pilot monthly invoice. This prevents outsized credits in extremely low-spend months.

I’ve copied Laura (Legal) to validate the carveout language. If that sounds reasonable I’ll produce a response redline and include our remedy matrix (remedy_budget_matrix.csv) showing concrete payout examples.

Would you be available for a 20-min call Thursday 13 Aug 10:00am PT to close?

— Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: CloudTerra SLA asks — legal review notes

Team — forwarding CloudTerra’s request and Mateo’s proposed position. Key legal points I’d tighten before sending a redline:

1) Maintenance carveouts: add a maximum allowed unnotified maintenance (cumulative) of 2 hours/month; everything else must be scheduled.
2) Fallback behavior: require that degraded-mode endpoints preserve request ordering and guarantee no dropped messages for pilot-critical routes; allow best-effort for non-critical bulk endpoints.
3) Remedy cap: OK to do lesser-of approach but explicitly exclude credits for agreed, scheduled maintenance.

Ben: can you run the proposed math in the remedy matrix against the pilot spend profile Mateo has and confirm the worst-case credit exposure? I want us to be comfortable if procurement pushes hard.

If we’re aligned, I’ll draft the formal redline for Mateo to send to CloudTerra.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 13 Aug 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: CloudTerra SLA asks — legal review notes

Quick run of numbers based on Mateo’s pilot forecast (estimated monthly invoice $45k):
- If cap = min($10k, 20% of invoice) -> 20% of $45k = $9,000 so effective cap = $9,000.
- Worst-case payout given a sustained 2% availability loss = ~$900 (assuming remedy scale in matrix).
- If traffic spikes double invoice for a month ($90k), 20% = $18k, cap enforces $10k -> protects our balance sheet.

Exposure looks acceptable for a 3-month pilot and gives procurement the predictability they want. Agree with legal on excluding scheduled maintenance. One ask from finance: add a clause for monthly reconciliation and one-time true-up within 30 days after pilot close.

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Finance, Redwood Inference
From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@cloudterra.com>, procurement@cloudterra.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 17:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Pilot SLA compromise proposal (CloudTerra)

Jordan — thanks for the patience while we reviewed internally. Summary of the pilot compromise Redwood can accept:

- Uptime baseline: 99.9% for the 3-month pilot only.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled windows up to 6 hours/month (72-hour notification). Unnotified maintenance allowance capped at 2 hours/month.
- Fallback behavior: critical routes will be routed to a compatible smaller model variant in degraded conditions (preserves ordering, no request drops). Non-critical bulk endpoints may be best-effort.
- Remedy cap: lesser of $10,000 or 20% of that month’s invoice; credits exclude scheduled maintenance.
- Monthly reconciliation & true-up: Redwood and CloudTerra will reconcile credits within 30 days following the pilot month; final adjustment at pilot close.

I’ve attached the redline (CloudTerra_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf) with our edits and the remedy budget CSV showing examples under a few invoice scenarios. If this aligns, we’ll send a DocuSign envelope for the pilot addendum and spin up the pilot environment next week.

Happy to discuss on a call tomorrow AM if you want to walk through details.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
